prompt: The most important aim of science should be to improve people’s lives. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this statement? Give reasons for your answer and include relevant examples from your knowledge or experience.
essay:
Scientific developments should always be aligned with and aimed at furthering the quality of human lives. I firmly agree with this statement, although for some reason, this purpose has not always been achieved. 

Sometimes scientists do research merely in the hope of expanding their knowledge, whereas the final results have been used for harmful purposes. Although they attempt their experiments would not harm individuals, they might not realize the consequences until the trials are finished. For example, Albert Einstein developed his famous theory to step forward in atomic physics but was unaware of the outcome to be applied to make a mass destructive bomb. In retrospect, we have also the scientist Nobel who aimed to serve mining workers by inventing dynamite which was regrettably used as a weapon afterwards. 

Most undoubtedly, there are firm arguments all of which are concerned with scientific discoveries improving human life. In these fields, the endeavours have solved individuals’ issues from the very beginning unquestionably. Besides, there were aims to create new resources in terms of remarkably improving the lifestyle level. For instance, electricity, and telecommunications are some innovations in this regard both of which are the outcome of years of experiments by scientists. Furthermore, the Internet, satellites, and smartphones would be named as the most recent ones all of which revolutionized lifestyles unprecedentedly. 

To conclude, knowledge and discovery have their own ways towards development and scientists are not always able to forecast how their breakthroughs will be used until the work is finalized.  However, I strongly believe science should improve the lives of people and that ought to be one of its main purposes.
